slides.title: Tell Me How
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 5 English, Unit 5: Tell Me How. Unit 5 turns you into a writer of instructions. You will take apart a Somali recipe for bariis to see how a title, a materials list, numbered steps and tips work together, and you will learn the zero conditional, the pattern that explains what happens every single time. Alongside the recipe you will read “The Memory Wall”, a story about a class who learn to communicate what matters to them. By the end you will have planned, drafted, tested and revised your own set of instructions that somebody else can genuinely follow. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Read procedural and instructional texts closely, naming their key features and explaining how the structure helps the reader.
Recognise imperative verbs such as rinse, stir, place and measure, and open your own written steps with them.
Identify and use time connectives such as first, next, then, after that and finally to sequence steps clearly.
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to read procedural and instructional texts closely, naming their key features and explaining how the structure helps the reader. You will also recognise imperative verbs such as rinse, stir, place and measure, and open your own written steps with them. You will also identify and use time connectives such as first, next, then, after that and finally to sequence steps clearly. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Language for precise thinking
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: communicate, quote, emphasise, persuade, convince, encourage. Listen to each pronunciation in the vocabulary lab, study its meaning in context, and use the word accurately in your own discussion and writing.

slides.title: Read critically
bullets: How to Make Bariis: Spiced Rice
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes What Makes Instructions Work and How to Make Bariis: Spiced Rice. Read actively. Identify each text's central ideas, notice viewpoint and reliability, and support every inference with relevant evidence from the text.

slides.title: What the Zero Conditional Is For
bullets: The zero conditional describes results that follow every single time. Scientists reach for it to state facts, and instruction writers reach for it to...
slides.narration: The first language focus is What the Zero Conditional Is For. The zero conditional describes results that follow every single time. Scientists reach for it to state facts, and instruction writers reach for it to explain what happens when a step is done properly or skipped. Notice the structure in the model examples, then apply it deliberately in connected sentences and paragraphs.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Explain, support and improve your ideas
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1: The Instruction Game (Pairs). Organise your ideas, use evidence and respond clearly to questions. In writing, you will plan, draft, check and revise. Use the success criteria before submitting your work.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the vocabulary lab, continue through reading and comprehension, apply the grammar focus, and complete the speaking and writing practices. Use AI English for hints and feedback any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
